audit_scope: Manual source/claim audit of Hastings-backed HTML notes only, using the supplied third-edition PDF and selected visual equation/figure inspection. Source text was read at the evidence pages listed. Broad chapter spans are surveyed via relevant passages; this is not a full independent verification of all1568 PDF pages or every textbook equation. Philis implementation was not audited.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Lithography, diffusion, implantation and etching create dimensions and surroundings that differ from drawn rectangles
citation_reviews.detail: Original span did not cover the contact/interconnect/CMP clauses. Added §2.7 PDF99–110; original span remains appropriate for front-end process mechanisms.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Manufacturing rules account for resolvability, process bias, registration, lateral diffusion/depletion and physical overlap
citation_reviews.detail: The process examples illustrate mechanisms. They are not current-node numerical rules; geometry and rule-construction discussion checked, not every example value.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Representative bipolar, CMOS and BiCMOS processes are teaching archetypes; sample rule values are not a real PDK
citation_reviews.detail: Checked chapter introduction and Appendix C disclaimer. This is a survey reference, not a claim that every process detail across the entire range was audited.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Representative bipolar, CMOS and BiCMOS processes are teaching archetypes; sample rule values are not a real PDK
citation_reviews.detail: Checked chapter introduction and Appendix C disclaimer. This is a survey reference, not a claim that every process detail across the entire range was audited.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Random variation, systematic biases, proximity and interconnect terms must not be collapsed into a single area law
citation_reviews.detail: Inverse-square-root area law is an areal-dominance approximation. Source includes peripheral contributions and process-specific coefficients.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Matching-rule grades are qualitative recommendations rather than universal numerical error guarantees
citation_reviews.detail: The book explains provisional guidance and limited quantitative data; notes appropriately demand process characterization.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: MOS matching objective depends on fixed voltage versus fixed current, operating region and active geometry
citation_reviews.detail: Long-channel strong-inversion formulas are scoped approximations; minimum-size/short-channel behavior is not inferred from them.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: General resistor-network centroid uses electrical sensitivity weights, not an unweighted bounding-box center
citation_reviews.detail: Visually checked Eqs8.24–8.25. Source example uses identical nominal resistor units and weights ∂Req/∂Ri. Ri∂Req/∂Ri for fractional perturbations is an explicitly derived extension.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: MOS gradient cancellation uses active gate-area centroids, not cell-outline centroids
citation_reviews.detail: Read §13.2.5 and Eq13.57 context; active-area weighting presumes local contribution and consistent operating assumptions.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Common-centroid layouts combine coincidence, symmetry, compactness and balanced subarrays; extra segmentation has costs
citation_reviews.detail: Source does not claim that every fine interdigitation cancels nonlinear gradients or that CC helps without a meaningful gradient.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Matched MOS arrays require equal signed current-direction orientation as well as centroid/symmetry constraints
citation_reviews.detail: Visually checked Eq13.61 and Table13.2. Equal nonzero means are permitted; +1/2 and −1/2 are not equal. SVG accessible description was corrected to match its 3:1 versus1:3 example.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Effective resistor geometry includes width/length bias, contact/end terms, corners and conductivity modulation
citation_reviews.detail: Eq6.10 gives 0.5587 squares for its ideal equal-width right-angle corner; not a process-independent corner model. Notes correctly distinguish identical-head cancellation from absolute error.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Resistor matching actions must control material, geometry, surroundings, fields, stress, heat and every lead material contribution
citation_reviews.detail: Checked source 25-rule catalog against the handbook mechanism table; table deliberately groups rules rather than duplicating names.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Contact-temperature differences produce signed thermoelectric voltages that common-centroid placement alone cannot cancel
citation_reviews.detail: Visually checked Eq8.34 and Fig8.22; cancellation depends on connection direction and matched temperature drops, not merely even segment count.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Resistor materials and trimming methods trade area, parasitics, power and stability
citation_reviews.detail: Checked relevant material/trim passages. A single-condition trim cannot generally remove other independent environmental errors; that limiting statement is synthesis, not a quoted universal source theorem.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Resistor matching actions must control material, geometry, surroundings, fields, stress, heat and every lead material contribution
citation_reviews.detail: Checked source 25-rule catalog against the handbook mechanism table; table deliberately groups rules rather than duplicating names.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Capacitor family, dielectric, bias and electrode construction affect nonlinearity, leakage, parasitics and loss
citation_reviews.detail: Family survey checked against relevant passages, not every material table. Port-role and PDK-model requirements are synthesis.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Capacitor matching uses appropriate identical parallel units, controlled perimeter/environment, dummies, shield reference and leads
citation_reviews.detail: Rules do not make series-connected units electrically identical to parallel units because electrode parasitics differ. X and Y pitch need not equal each other.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Lead resistance and capacitance can defeat body matching; compare actual connection topology and environment
citation_reviews.detail: Electrical equivalence matters more than equal drawn length. The numerical capacitor example assumes the added parasitics are parallel to the intended measured capacitances.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: MOS matching objective depends on fixed voltage versus fixed current, operating region and active geometry
citation_reviews.detail: Long-channel strong-inversion formulas are scoped approximations; minimum-size/short-channel behavior is not inferred from them.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: MOS matching rules require same unit construction and qualified dummies/environment plus thermal/package/bias control
citation_reviews.detail: Qualitative matching grades and old numerical suggestions are not universal process requirements. Notes retain these qualifiers.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Matched MOS arrays require equal signed current-direction orientation as well as centroid/symmetry constraints
citation_reviews.detail: Visually checked Eq13.61 and Table13.2. Equal nonzero means are permitted; +1/2 and −1/2 are not equal. SVG accessible description was corrected to match its 3:1 versus1:3 example.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Physical relative orientation and terminal-directed geometry must be preserved within a matched group
citation_reviews.detail: Source explicitly recommends grouping matched devices to avoid independent rotation; mirrored asymmetric devices need qualification.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Gate etch, dummies, WPE, trench/LOD stress, bias and hydrogenation make local MOS surroundings electrically relevant
citation_reviews.detail: Corrected LOD figure locator: discussion697, actual Fig13.52 is698. Example effect magnitudes and signs are not universal.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: MOS matching rules require same unit construction and qualified dummies/environment plus thermal/package/bias control
citation_reviews.detail: Qualitative matching grades and old numerical suggestions are not universal process requirements. Notes retain these qualifiers.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: BJT random/systematic matching depends on emitter geometry, current density, bias, thermal environment and connection effects
citation_reviews.detail: Matched unit construction and cautions are source-backed. Numerical thermal and beta examples are explicitly hypothetical circuit derivations.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Lateral BJT perimeter, collector arrangement and field environment differ from vertical-emitter area scaling
citation_reviews.detail: A larger emitter is not automatically a better lateral PNP; the notes preserve the device-family distinction.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Thermal and terminal/beta effects can turn a nominal current ratio into a VBE error
citation_reviews.detail: Checked bias/temperature mechanisms and independently recomputed the 8:1, 1%, beta-ratio and 50mK examples. No example temperature coefficient is represented as universal.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: BJT matching rules require controlled geometry, temperature/stress and parasitic interactions
citation_reviews.detail: Reverse emitter-base avalanche and shared-region/depletion cautions remain device/process dependent.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: PN, Schottky and Zener matching cannot share a single generic diode objective
citation_reviews.detail: Source distinguishes emitter versus collector current and nonuniform avalanche conduction.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Paralleled Zener segments can share avalanche current nonuniformly rather than average like ordinary passive units
citation_reviews.detail: Source mechanism checked; no Pelgrom-style universal Zener improvement is claimed.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Schottky material/barrier/contact/field geometry and guard-junction bias affect leakage, voltage and minority injection
citation_reviews.detail: Added §11.2 PDF563 to directly support the forward-biased field-relief guard-junction injection clause. Original matching span alone was incomplete.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Inductor performance depends on winding resistance, frequency effects, substrate/metal surroundings, shielding and parasitic capacitance
citation_reviews.detail: §7.2.1–2 supports EM-environment constraints. Q≈ωL/R and the ideal LC resonance example are stated as simplified circuit estimates, not as a universal extracted model.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Power bipolar devices require debiasing, ballast and electrothermal/SOA analysis appropriate to their switching regime
citation_reviews.detail: Checked central power-device mechanisms. Broad source span also covers detailed structures not reproduced in notes.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: MOS power layouts combine silicon/metal/package R, distributed gate delay, body resistance, SOA and SenseFET environment
citation_reviews.detail: Source-backed mechanism survey. The approximate distributed-finger equation is separately audited; SenseFET pattern proposals require extraction and bias/thermal equivalence.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: A uniform distributed, singly terminated finger has small-debiasing added metal resistance about one third of end-to-end wire resistance
citation_reviews.detail: Visually checked AppendixE. E.6 sign, E.8 conductance prefactor and E.14 missing square root are apparent source inconsistencies; corrected model derived from E.3–E.4 and agrees with E.9. Source errata are unconfirmed by publisher.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: A uniform distributed, singly terminated finger has small-debiasing added metal resistance about one third of end-to-end wire resistance

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Annular, EEPROM and JFET structures require their own process-qualified geometry and operating constraints
citation_reviews.detail: Broad specialty survey checked by relevant passages, not a full construction manual.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: High-voltage MOS operation depends on drift regions, field distribution, body/isolation and safe operating area
citation_reviews.detail: Checked physical argument and device construction constraints, not every high-voltage example. Automatic transformations remain PDK-qualified.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Heat, current density, dielectric stress, processing charge and parasitic conduction require separate reliability checks
citation_reviews.detail: Broad mechanism survey checked through the relevant subsections. Scenario-based verification procedure is handbook synthesis; no numerical foundry rule is inferred.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: ESD protection is a coordinated primary/secondary circuit with complete discharge and return paths
citation_reviews.detail: Broad survey checked at relevant source mechanisms, not every device topology. Qualified library cells and testing remain required.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Antenna damage depends on fabrication-stage connectivity and exposed conducting geometry; later-metal jumps and diodes mitigate different stages
citation_reviews.detail: Stage graph, metrics and worked 180-to-20 example are explicit handbook proposals/illustrations, not an algorithm printed in Hastings. Area/perimeter metric must follow the process.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Clipping, snapback and rate-triggered primary protection have different allowed-operation and secondary-protection requirements
citation_reviews.detail: Local protected terminals/reference and intentional limiting impedance must be preserved.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Secondary protection, multifinger ballasting and reverse-BE avalanche degradation matter for analog accuracy
citation_reviews.detail: Read direct mechanism passages. The 7V+IR+Ldi/dt example is independently derived and explicitly illustrative.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Majority taps, minority-carrier collecting junctions and blocking barriers are distinct; depth, bias and continuity control guard effectiveness
citation_reviews.detail: Read detailed §5.4.4, including qualified L/U collecting guards near die edges and closed blocking barriers. Does not imply every ring is interchangeable.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Guard choice and effectiveness depend on substrate doping, buried layers, depth, contact resistance and allowed bias
citation_reviews.detail: Source examples are strongly process dependent; numerical collection efficiencies are not copied as universal thresholds.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Device sharing can introduce minority-carrier injection, common-resistance debiasing and capacitively mediated errors
citation_reviews.detail: Whitelist/re-extract transformation procedure is original synthesis. The source supports why schematic net equality alone is insufficient.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Noisy isolated MOS transistors can inject into shared tanks and disturb sensitive circuits
citation_reviews.detail: Read explicit warning about parasitic rectification and shared-tank coupling.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: A Kelvin/star connection must join physically at the intended reference; sharing a net name does not remove IR drop
citation_reviews.detail: Read Figures15.26–15.27 and text; finite sense current and common path matter.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Capacitive coupling depends on slew and victim impedance; shielding requires a suitable low-impedance reference
citation_reviews.detail: Eq15.23 is an illustrative lumped relation. Notes do not promise that a shield removes all coupling or that a logically static net has no startup transitions.

citation_reviews.supported_claim: Local neck/via current density can dominate reliability although total resistance integrates along the path
citation_reviews.detail: Visually checked Fig15.29. An inside-corner via array does not share current uniformly; straight transitions reduce the illustrated nonuniformity.

citation_reviews.detail: Not all via families stack legally. Worked 100+100 pitch versus140 landing example is explicit arithmetic under hypothetical dimensions.

unresolved: No claim of full accuracy or complete exhaustive textbook coverage is justified. The audit covers the stated handbook claims and selected source passages, with broad survey references marked qualified.
Apparent AppendixE E.6/E.8/E.14 errors were found by equation/dimensional checks; publisher confirmation or an errata sheet was not obtained. Use the explicitly derived consistent model.
PDK/device/package-specific magnitudes, signs, limits and coefficient fits remain external evidence requirements. Textbook examples cannot serve as foundry qualification.

Many handbook structures—scenario ledgers, dependency invalidation, optimization schemas and suggested algorithms—are original synthesis from physical mechanisms. They must not be cited as an algorithm implemented or proven in Hastings.

The specialty RF/HV/JFET/EEPROM and historical-process material is a survey of layout implications, not an exhaustive construction manual. Do not infer qualified generators or full coverage of every device variant.
No direct Hastings source for sampled kT/C noise or 4kTR was found in searchable text. Do not attribute those equations to this source without another verified locator.
No direct Hastings formula P/(2πκr) was found. Fourier Eq8.22 provides governing context, but half-space point-source assumptions and integration must be stated as a derivation.
material_omissions: No omitted Hastings matching-rule category was found in the audited resistor/capacitor/MOS catalogs. This does not establish that every relevant source topic is fully taught. Detailed RF electromagnetic construction, every process recipe, all specialized HV/ESD structures and PDK qualification remain intentionally survey-level.

theory_records.title: Random matching is not one universal area law
theory_records.claim: Separate statistical variation from systematic offsets; areal and peripheral variation contribute differently, with inverse-square-root area only in the areal-dominant regime.
theory_records.assumptions: Process/material/model coefficients and valid device dimensions must be characterized; differently sized units can be dominated by the smaller unit.

theory_records.title: Electrical sensitivity defines the relevant centroid
theory_records.claim: A resistor-network centroid is weighted by its sensitivity to unit resistance, rather than by cell outline or instance count.
theory_records.assumptions: Source example uses identical nominal resistors subject to equal absolute perturbation. A fractional perturbation generalization weights Ri·∂Req/∂Ri and is a chain-rule extension, not Eq8.24 verbatim.

theory_records.title: Common centroid has conditions and implementation costs
theory_records.claim: Coincidence, symmetry, compactness and balanced subarrays reduce specified gradient errors; excessive segmentation can reduce active area and worsen random matching.
theory_records.assumptions: Linear-field cancellation is first order. Curved fields, routing/end terms and fixed footprint require a separate error budget; no-gradient cases gain no gradient benefit.

theory_records.title: MOS signed orientation must match
theory_records.claim: For identical MOS sections with horizontal channel current, orientation is the mean of ±1 current directions. Matched arrays require equal signed means; equal nonzero means are allowed.
theory_records.assumptions: Identical unit sections and electrical terminal directions; in two dimensions compare both components. Relative geometric rotation alone is insufficient.

theory_records.title: MOS current matching depends on bias and geometry
theory_records.claim: Long-channel saturation has ID=kVov²/2, gm=√(2kID), k=k′We/Le; the mismatch observable differs between fixed gate voltage and fixed drain current.
theory_records.assumptions: Strong inversion, long-channel model; ignore CLM/velocity saturation only when justified. Use effective rather than blindly drawn geometry. Current/gate bias assumptions must accompany derived sensitivities.

theory_records.title: WPE and LOD encode different local environments
theory_records.claim: Well implant scattering, trench stress and length-of-diffusion/end geometry can change otherwise nominally identical MOS devices.
theory_records.locator: §13.2.2 Diffusion, Implantation, Etch, and Trench Effects; Figs13.49–13.52
theory_records.assumptions: PDK-specific mechanism magnitude/sign and device polarity; preserve actual edge distances or qualified dummies. Fig13.52 is physical PDF698.

theory_records.title: Dummies need process and electrical meaning
theory_records.claim: Matched MOS edges require suitable gate/dummy neighborhood and overhang; half/full dummies and inactive terminal ties are not interchangeable.
theory_records.assumptions: Use qualified dummy extent/pitch and safe terminal bias. Added rectangles do not automatically reproduce the active device environment.

theory_records.title: Metal fill can perturb passivation and matching
theory_records.claim: Metal above or near matched MOS regions can change hydrogenation/passivation and environmental symmetry.
theory_records.assumptions: Process-dependent hydrogen transport/material stack; source numerical distances and preferences are not generic modern-node mandates. Fill also has extraction-dependent electrical effects. Handbook workflow implication: final fill must be included when rechecking affected geometry and electrical behavior; that lifecycle policy is our derivation from the physical mechanism.

theory_records.title: Resistor physical geometry includes end and corner terms
theory_records.claim: Unequal widths turn common process bias into ratio error; contacts/heads/corners must be matched or modeled. An ideal equal-width right-angle corner is 0.5587 squares.
theory_records.assumptions: The corner result assumes the source ideal sheet/current-boundary geometry. Real contact and process-biased corners require calibrated models; identical systematic heads can cancel.

theory_records.title: Thermoelectric cancellation is a connection problem
theory_records.claim: ET=SΔTC describes the net contact-temperature EMF; series sections can add or cancel it depending on electrical traversal. Common-centroid placement alone cannot cancel it.
theory_records.assumptions: Matched material Seebeck behavior and temperature drops; opposite path directions must be paired. An even segment count alone does not guarantee cancellation in an arbitrary field.

theory_records.title: Precision resistor leads must scale by material
theory_records.claim: Metal, contact and via contributions can change an intended resistor ratio; for ratioed devices each material contribution should preserve the ratio or be budgeted separately.
theory_records.assumptions: Different lead materials have different temperature coefficients. Equal body R ratios or equal route lengths alone do not establish terminal ratios.

theory_records.title: Capacitor ratios need perimeter and topology control
theory_records.claim: Identical parallel units control ratio errors from area and periphery; series interconnection introduces different electrode-parasitic behavior.
theory_records.assumptions: Fixed capacitor family and actual plate connections; nonunit geometries must match sensitivity rather than merely nominal C.

theory_records.title: Capacitor plate roles and surroundings matter
theory_records.claim: Capacitor electrodes can have asymmetric substrate/interconnect parasitics; edge dummies and shields need intentional quiet connections and balanced surroundings.
theory_records.assumptions: Real terminal roles, finite shield impedance, bias and surrounding noise matter. Dummies cannot be assigned arbitrary floating or noisy potentials.

theory_records.title: BJT matching is device-family specific
theory_records.claim: Vertical emitters, lateral emitter perimeters, beta/base-current errors, collector bias and thermal gradients demand different matching checks.
theory_records.assumptions: Identify matched observable and operating region; same total area does not make a lateral device equivalent, and reverse-BE stress can degrade accuracy.

theory_records.title: Do not merge diode matching models
theory_records.claim: PN current definition, Schottky field/barrier construction and nonuniform Zener avalanche produce different matching/injection behavior.
theory_records.assumptions: Schottky guard-junction forward bias can inject minority carriers; Zener segments may current-hog. Do not assume ordinary unit-area averaging applies to avalanche.

theory_records.title: Antenna checking follows fabrication stages
theory_records.claim: Plasma damage depends on the conductive geometry connected to a gate during each process stage; later-layer jumpers and protective diodes address different exposed-node situations.
theory_records.assumptions: Foundry defines gate denominator, exposed area/perimeter, layer accumulation and diode credit. Final net connectivity is insufficient; stage-graph implementation is handbook synthesis.

theory_records.title: Guard rings require carrier, depth and return-path context
theory_records.claim: Collecting PN junctions, high-low blocking regions and majority taps have different functions; minority carriers can bypass shallow guards or debias weak returns.
theory_records.assumptions: Qualified geometry/bias/substrate stack required. Blocking guards need appropriate complete 3D barriers; special collecting L/U guards near die edges are not generalized to blockers.

theory_records.title: ESD protection must coordinate actual terminal voltages
theory_records.claim: Clipping, snapback and rate-triggered protectors require different operating constraints; secondary protection must use the vulnerable device local reference and qualified limiting paths.
theory_records.assumptions: Normal supply/slew/failsafe conditions, stress polarity and tested cell topology matter. Multifinger width does not imply uniform current; local ballast may be intentional.

theory_records.title: Local current density sets reliability bottlenecks
theory_records.claim: Via arrays and bent leads need current-distribution analysis: inner-corner vias can carry far more current than outer ones.
theory_records.assumptions: Foundry lifetime model, material/interface, local temperature and waveform determine limits. Total via count and average wire width are insufficient.

theory_records.title: Physical Kelvin junctions and victim impedance matter
theory_records.claim: Shared-path voltage drops persist on one named net; capacitive disturbance depends on aggressor slew and victim impedance, while shields need an effective reference.
theory_records.locator: §15.4.4 Special Routing Techniques, Figs15.26–15.28 and Eq15.23
theory_records.assumptions: Use actual branch topology and local references. Eq15.23 is a simplified lumped relation; frequency-dependent impedances and return paths may require extraction.

theory_records.title: Manufacturable pitch includes enclosure and registration
theory_records.claim: Design-rule margins account for fabrication deviations; routing pitch must allow legal via/contact landing geometry, not only drawn line width plus nominal line spacing.
theory_records.locator: §3.2.3 Design Rule Construction; §15.4.2 Eqs15.18–15.20; AppendixC disclaimer
theory_records.assumptions: Numeric textbook rules are teaching examples. Use actual PDK shape/grid/stacking rules and qualified waivers; geometry needs to be checked after generation.

theory_records.title: Exact distributed-finger model before the one-third limit
theory_records.claim: For constant r,g and a singly terminated finger of length L, Rtotal=RSi·u·coth(u), u=L√(rg); small u gives added metal R≈rL/3.
theory_records.assumptions: Uniform geometry and distributed silicon conductance; v(0)=V, i(L)=0. Not a generic bound for tapered/strongly nonuniform devices. Supplied E.6 sign, E.8 prefactor and E.14 sqrt appear inconsistent.
theory_records.derivation_if_any: Solve v′=−ri and i′=−gv with open far-end boundary: i(0)=√(g/r)V tanh(L√(rg)); invert and use g=1/(LRSi). Expand ucothu=1+u²/3−u⁴/45+…. This agrees with source E.9; correction is audit algebra, not publisher-confirmed erratum.

theory_records.title: RF passive surroundings are part of the device
theory_records.claim: Skin/proximity loss, eddy currents, capacitance and surrounding metal determine frequency-dependent inductor quality; patterned shields must interrupt induced loops.
theory_records.assumptions: Use frequency-dependent port/EM models and qualified fill exclusions. Parallel metal stacking differs from series winding layers; more turns/width is not universally better.

theory_records.title: Power MOS layout needs dynamic and thermal checks
theory_records.claim: Distributed gate resistance/capacitance causes nonuniform switching; body resistance and electrothermal feedback can localize current even when on-resistance has a positive temperature coefficient in another regime.
theory_records.locator: §13.1.2 Switching Losses, Eqs13.21–13.23/Figs13.8–13.10; §13.1.3 SOA; §13.1.4 SenseFET discussion
theory_records.assumptions: Waveform, bias, package heat path and process determine SOA. SenseFET layout must sample representative terminal voltages/temperature; repeated small-signal units alone do not establish power capability.

theory_records.title: Thermal-gradient theory needs boundary conditions
theory_records.claim: Heat flux follows Fourier’s law q=−κ∇T; package-dependent 3D heat flow and active-region weighting determine how temperature gradients affect matching.
theory_records.locator: §5.1.1 Self-Heating, Eq5.6 finite source and Eqs5.7–5.9; §8.2.7 Temperature Eq8.22 and Eq8.23 context
theory_records.assumptions: Active-centroid model assumes local/planar contribution, suitable linear temperature response and a linear field. P/(2πκr) is not found verbatim in this book; a half-space point-source use must be labeled an independent Fourier-law derivation with its own boundaries.

independent_confirmation: Physics auditor independently rendered AppendixE871–872 and confirmed all three algebraic inconsistencies. At u=1, metal-only one-third error is6.48% although total-R error is1.546%; notes intentionally do not reuse the source threshold as a metal-only guarantee.

new_direct_citations_checked.claim: HCI degradation depends on operating bias/time; source236 and238 directly checked.
NBTI/PBTI threshold/transconductance degradation and bias/temperature/recovery dependence.
Illustrative historical rule tables are not a real process.
